newsitem.title: USA: Lucent to develop new monitor for Nielsen. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lucent to develop new monitor for Nielsen. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]

text.p: Nielsen Media Research of Cognizant Corp. said Monday that Lucent Technologies Inc. will develop a better system for the company to monitor television audiences, especially in the advent of digital television.

A spokesman for Nielsen, known for its television viewership ratings, said Lucent would develop a new monitoring system to help Nielsen determine the most popular television programs, among other uses (corrects by eliminating the word "replace").
He said the system would be used for both analogue and digital television, as well as the Internet.

The spokesman said the agreement also called for both companies to share information. Nielsen will share software and methodology used to monitor things like television viewership and advertising expenditures. Lucent will share its digital compression system, which would enable a broadcaster to offer more than one programme at the same time on one channel, he said.

Nielsen, based in New York City, has developed a new metering system in anticipation of the transition to DTV. Lucent has been developing DTV encoding and decoding products for use in the consumer electronics marketplace.
Murray Hill, N.J.-based Lucent's stock fell 25 cents to $71.56, while Nielsen rose 37.5 cents to $37.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
